articleTitle: Class-D audio power amplifiers: an overview
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The advances in semiconductor technology have renewed interest in class-D audio amplifiers, especially for portable devices, and consumer electronics. This paper gives an overview of where class-D amplifiers are being used today, and why.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal edge-based median filtering for deinterlacing
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new computationally efficient deinterlacing algorithm which shows effective visual performance. In the proposed scheme, correlation dependent interpolation and line doubling schemes are utilized separately for the low frequency and high frequency components of the 2-D input signal. Computer simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm shows better visual performance than conventional deinterlacing algorithms.

articleTitle: Home gateway architecture and its implementation
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We proposed the home gateway architecture. We have implemented the Web server based home gateway, interconnecting IEEE 1394, the powerline home automation network, and the Internet, with real-time AV transcoding capability.

articleTitle: DVD+RW: 2-way compatibility for video and data applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper discusses the 4.7-GB digital versatile disc plus rewritable (DVD+RW) system as a future replacement for the video cassette recorder (VCR). It is shown that the digital versatile discs can be recorded in a fully compatible manner with the existing DVD-video standard and players. The compatibility issue is addressed from the perspective of the DVD-video physical and logical formats.

articleTitle: Improved vein pattern extracting algorithm and its implementation
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved vein pattern extracting algorithm which compensates the loss of vein patterns in the edge area, gives more enhanced and stabilized vein pattern information, and shows better performance than the existing algorithm. Also, the problem arising from the iterative nature of the filtering preprocess in the existing algorithm is solved by designing a filter that is processed only one time so that a fast recognition speed and reduced hardware complexity is obtained. The proposed algorithm is implemented with a FPGA (field programmable gate array) device and the FAR (false acceptance rate) shows five times batter than the existing algorithm and the recognition speed is measured to be 100 [ms/person].

articleTitle: A novel drive architecture of HDD: "multimode hard disc drive"
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The newly introduced "multimode hard disc drive" architecture, capable of ultra-high speed data transfer, low power consumption, AV/data partitioning among others, is shown to be a viable drive architecture with high potentiality for AV/IT applications.

articleTitle: Automated test system for digital TV receivers
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The quality of a digital TV receiver is related to the quality of the images it produces. This paper describes the design of an automated test system for testing the image quality of digital TV receivers.

articleTitle: A low-cost audio/video single-chip MPEG2 encoder for consumer video storage applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes a low cost single-chip MPEG2 audio/video encoder for consumer storage applications. The IC performs sophisticated noise reduction, IPB video encoding, MPEG or AC3 stereo audio-encoding and system multiplexing. Furthermore it has low resource demands both in terms of SDRAM bandwidth and silicon area. Thus it delivers a true low cost solution, whilst maintaining superior video quality.

articleTitle: Visual program navigation system based on spatial distribution of color
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a visual program navigation system using our proposals for MPEG-7, these are adopted as MPEG-7 XM. MPEG-7 supports two levels of description, a low-level and a high-level. The former is designed to capture signal processing based features, and the latter is intended to represent semantic features. We show an implementation example of a personalized digital recorder (PDR) application, which uses both levels. It uses a color layout descriptor for image retrieval. The image retrieval efficiency is quite high in spite of its high-speed retrieval with low cost description. A content personalization interface is also implemented using a set of meta information and provides a variety of content visualization functions.

articleTitle: Silicon single-chip television tuner technology
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A family of silicon single-chip television tuners has been developed. We have characterized these devices and present the data. Two applications have been developed employing the IC tuner. These are a PCI add-in card for a PC so that the PC may receive and display TV signals, and a module that provides for bi-directional communication over a cable system.

articleTitle: VNA: an object model for virtual network appliances
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a new architecture for integrating networked appliances, called virtual network appliance (VNA). Instead of merely connecting appliances seen in existing approaches, the VNA architecture enables users to create a networked appliance by assembling functional components of existing appliances. Users can achieve dynamic adaptation and personal customization, exploiting VNA.

articleTitle: Noise measurement in video images
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Many image enhancement algorithms easily fail in the presence of noise. Noise adaptive algorithms are much more robust, and a good and accurate enough algorithm for noise measurement is a key component. The proposed algorithms combine good performance with low complexity.

articleTitle: Automatic extraction of facial feature points for MPEG4 videophone applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of automatically extracting a set of characteristic feature points from images containing a front view of a human face. These feature points include edge-points of the basic characteristics of a face and are extremely useful for the adaptation of 3D head models and the extraction of facial animation parameters of the synthetic/natural hybrid coding (SNHC) part of the MPEG4 image coding standard. The proposed method is based on: (a) an initial segmentation of the chrominance image to extract a rough area of the face, (b) post-processing of the extracted area by standard dilation and erosion operators, (c) geometric region splitting within the facial area and (d) detection of the features within their corresponding regions based on their geometrical characteristics.

articleTitle: A robust DCT-based watermarking for copyright protection
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A novel method for embedding watermarks into a host image in the frequency domain is proposed. Unlike the traditional techniques, the method addresses that watermark is embedded into the lower frequency. The watermark is self-extractable and the algorithm is simple. Experimental results demonstrate that the watermark is robust to various attacks.

articleTitle: Digital audio watermarking in the cepstrum domain
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Watermarking is a technique used to label digital media by hiding copyright or other information into the underlying data. The watermark must be imperceptible and undetectable by the user and should be robust to various types of distortion. We propose a new algorithm for digital audio watermarking in the cepstrum domain, where we insert a watermark into the cepstral components of the audio signal using techniques analogous to spread spectrum communications, hiding a narrow band signal in a wideband channel.

articleTitle: A low-complexity MPEG-2 bit-rate transcoding algorithm
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes a low complexity MPEG-2 bitrate transcoding algorithm that achieves an extra compression factor of about two without introducing annoying coding artefacts. Due to the low complexity of this algorithm it is especially applicable in DSP/CPU software solutions or in consumer applications that require high throughput.

articleTitle: Architecture for a digital video recorder
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The continuously declining price of the hard disk drive presents the opportunity for digital disk-based systems to displace tape- and analog-based systems for consumers video storage needs by the end of the decade. This paper discusses the requirements of such a system and an integrated circuit designed to help these products reach an aggressive price target.

articleTitle: Evolution of dynamic gaits for a robot
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: An evolutionary algorithm is used to evolve dynamic gaits for the Sony pet-type robot and for AIBO(R). All processing is handled by the robots' on-board computer with individuals evaluated using the robots' sensors. Our implementation successfully evolves trot and pace gaits for which the pace gait significantly outperforms previous hand-developed gaits. Using this technique we evolved the trot gait used in the consumer version of AIBO.

articleTitle: An FPGA-based video compressor for H.263 compatible bitstreams
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents an architecture for video encoding according to the H.263 standard for video conference systems. The implementation is based on an commercial available FPGA and is embedded in a PCI plug-in card with on-board SRAM plus external SRAM. The most complex part of the H.263 protocol, a base-line encoder, could already be implemented and is able to operate at 30 MHz. This leads to a maximum compression speed of 120 Mbit/s allowing simultaneous real-time procession of several video streams in a single reconfigurable chip. Soon the progress of FPGA integration density will make it possible to implement coding options, too. The use of FPGA technology enables adapting the hardware to various protocols and environments by software and therefore to save development time and hardware costs.

articleTitle: A universal DTV chip set for US/Japan digital TV broadcast
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A novel chip set for US/Japan DTV is described. It consists of a flexible HD-MPEG AN decoder, a powerful format converter/graphics processor, high performance 8PSK/OFDM demodulators, and 1394 digital interface.

articleTitle: A fast full search motion estimation algorithm using the sum of partial norms
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a fast block motion estimation algorithm using the sum of partial norms which finds the same motion vectors as the exhaustive full search algorithm with a reduced computational load. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is about 3 or 4 times faster than the original exhaustive full search, and is about 2 times faster than the successive elimination algorithm (SEA).

articleTitle: Image encryption for secure Internet multimedia applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We present a novel scheme for secure Internet image transmission. The feature of the proposed scheme is joint application between image compression and image encryption. For source coding, we implement the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and for channel coding, we utilize the block cipher Data Encryption Standard (DES) algorithm. Simulation results show that our proposed method significantly enhances security for image transmission over Internet as well as improves the transmission rate.

articleTitle: An innovative, high quality and search window independent motion estimation algorithm and architecture for MPEG-2 encoding
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes an innovative, pipelined, cache-based architecture for a motion estimation coprocessor. The coprocessor is based on a predictive/recursive algorithm whose computational complexity is low and not dependent on the search window. The synergies between the architecture and algorithm's features allow a high picture quality, low-area, low-bandwidth, unlimited search window implementation.

articleTitle: Color transient improvement (CTI)
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We describe the color transient improvement (CTI) involving the detection and sharpening the edges in chrominance. CTI algorithm works purely on the U and V data within a frame, modifying this data where necessary to sharpen U and V transients. The CTI algorithm works on the U and V data independently.

articleTitle: Auto focus filter design and implementation using correlation between filter and auto focus criterion
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A new filter design method for an auto focus is proposed which can be implemented into a simple hardware. The proposed auto focus filter can be implemented without multipliers. Therefore, we can sharply reduce the number of filter coefficients by the proposed design method. The proposed filter design method is simulated and tested by our hardware system.

articleTitle: An innovative low complexity MPEG-2 video transcoder operating in the DCT domain
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A novel method to transcode the MPEG-2 bitstream in order to reduce its flow is presented together with its architecture. It is a method of great flexibility and very low complexity. It needs a low amount of memory and can be easily integrated in the global architecture. Rate reduction can be gradually achieved from any value allowed by the selected MPEG-2 profile to any lower rate. Compared to a decoder-encoder pipeline, the quality of the transcoded bitstream is equal or even better, being very close to the quality achieved by encoding the source signal at the target bitrate. Furthermore, the hardware complexity is fairly lower, requiring less than 10 mm/sup 2/ in 0.25 /spl mu/m technology.

articleTitle: Content-based navigation of television programs using MPEG-7 description schemes
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes a prototype system for content-based navigation of television programs based on MPEG-7. It proposes an automatic algorithm for generating MPEG-7 description data for television news programs, integrating audio and visual information.

articleTitle: Enhancement of region-of-interest coded images by using adaptive regularization
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a new algorithm that post-processes wavelet-based ROI coded images by using adaptive iterative regularization. The proposed algorithm can efficiently reduce the ringing artifacts as well as restore the details of the image. The algorithm can be used in still image compression standards, videophone, video conferencing, and other visual communication systems.

articleTitle: Performance of an advanced video codec on a general-purpose processor with media ISA extensions
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper analyses the performance of the state-of-the-art media ISA (instruction set architecture) extensions in a general-purpose processor, when executing a video encoder based on an affine motion model.

articleTitle: TV anytime: STORit on myTV
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper discusses provider-guided storage of content local storage device to implement TV anytime features. The work is being carried out in two projects: STORit and myTV. Both projects are funded by the European Commission.

articleTitle: An algorithm for integrated noise reduction and sharpness enhancement
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Noise filters tend to blur image detail, while filters for image sharpening tend to increase noise. So, cascading the two filters does not always give the best performance. We present an integrated filter that reduces noise or sharpens details in a noisy video signal, depending on local image statistics.

articleTitle: A unified approach to scene change detection in uncompressed and compressed video
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: There is an urgent need to extract key information automatically from video for the purposes of indexing, fast retrieval and scene analysis. To support this vision, reliable scene change detection algorithms must be developed. This paper describes a novel unified algorithm for scene change detection in uncompressed and MPEG-2 compressed video sequences using statistical features of images. Results on video of various content types are reported and validated with the proposed scheme in uncompressed and MPEG-2 compressed video. Furthermore, results show that the accuracy of the detected transitions is above 95% and 90% for uncompressed and MPEG-2 compressed video respectively.

articleTitle: An MPEG-2 encoding PC card system for real-time mobile applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes an MPEG-2 real-time encoding Type-II PC card system for mobile applications. It incorporates a new hardware/software cooperative architecture for synchronizing audio data and video data in real-time.

articleTitle: Truncated metric for NTSC interference rejection in the ATSC-HDTV trellis decoder
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes a family of metrics with better performance than the Euclidean metric in the NTSC co-channel interference case of the ATSC-HDTV trellis decoder.

articleTitle: Using asymmetric digital subscriber line (ADSL) for fast Internet and multimedia services
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this paper the design of an experimental ADSL network and the applications used are presented. Digital subscriber line (DSL) technologies enable the use of twisted pair copper telephone lines, that reach practically every home and business (public switched telephone network) with very large bandwidth, typically from 1.5-6 Mbps downstream and 640 kbps upstream, by placing a pair of modems at the user (home) and at the C.O. (PTT Central Office) side. After a small introduction on broadband access networks the design of an experimental ADSL network is presented. Furthermore, the design of high bandwidth, rich in content applications taking advantage of the high speed ADSL network is given.

articleTitle: Fingerprint verification system with improved image enhancement and reliable matching
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper deals with a fingerprint verification system (FVS), which consists of extracting and matching of minutiae from the input image. We present an improved fingerprint enhancement algorithm, which can improve the clarity of the ridge and valley structure. We also propose a fast and reliable minutiae matching algorithm, capable of finding the correspondences between minutiae in the input image and the stored template without a exhaustive search. A standalone FVS system is implemented with ADSP21060, FPGA, memory and live-scan input device.

articleTitle: Enhancing the DOCSIS cable modem specifications with an advanced physical layer for upstream transmission
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The effective capacity and the immunity to noise and impairments of upstream transmissions in a DOCSIS system can be enhanced through the use of an advanced physical layer. Such improvements are valuable for deployment of advanced services. In addition, these improvements serve to increase the number of cable systems around the world that provide a transmission environment ready to sustain successful operation of DOCSIS communications channels. This paper indicates how a specific spread-spectrum technology, called synchronous code division multiple access (S-CDMA), can be incorporated into DOCSIS-based systems. The potential inclusion of S-CDMA as an evolutionary enhancement to DOCSIS provides backward compatibility with existing DOCSIS systems and equipment. The paper shows how this requirement can be met using the same physical channel. The theory of operation of S-CDMA is provided, along with analysis and simulation results showing the improvements that can be obtained. S-CDMA is also compared with other technologies that may also play a role in extending the capabilities of the DOCSIS upstream physical layer.

articleTitle: Optimization of transceiver systems for broadband fixed wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Systems designed for high data rate broadband wireless multimedia services must combat fading and multipath impairments. In this paper, the effects of these impairments on transceiver signal processing system design are analyzed, and the system architecture of spatial transmit diversity combined with adaptive modulation is presented. The performance of such a system is compared with conventional single carrier fixed modulation and OFDM systems.

articleTitle: Format detection for DVD+ReWritable 4.7 GB
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents the fundamentals of the DVD+ReWritable 4.7 GB (DVD+RW) groove format of the disk. It describes the format detection and addresses the IC implementation of the required circuitry. Simulation and measurement results show the robustness of both the DVD+RW groove format of the disk and of the applied format detection method and circuitry.

articleTitle: Digital amplification for consumer audio
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper overviews the emerging important field of digital power amplification for audio. Since most of the solutions presented in the open literature rely on pulse width modulation, this is our main focus.

articleTitle: The cellular mobile IPv6 using low latency handoff algorithm for the packet-based cellular network
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this paper, cellular mobile IPv6 (CMI) a new algorithm that is migrated from mobile IPv6 is proposed for mobile nodes moving among small wireless cells at high speed. It is important for future mobile communication environments and should eventually integrate its functions with the Internet. The purpose of this paper is to solve the problems of a communication break within a smaller cellular coverage during high-speed movement with packet switched data or the real-time voice messages. Thus, voice over IP (VoIP) packets were chosen to implement the system. Simulation results show a smooth and non-breaking handoff during high-speed movement using the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Comparison of two modulation techniques using frequency domain processing in interference limited home networks
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Previous developments show an increasing interest for wireless in-house multimedia communication within the 2.4 GHz ISM-band. A disadvantage of the ISM-band is the high level of mainly narrowband interference, generated by other communication systems and by the leakage of microwave ovens. Good communication is therefore only possible when appropriate measures are taken to compensate for the interference. We compare the performance of two different modulation techniques in the presence of narrowband interference. We consider OFDM and single-carrier modulation with frequency domain processing. A static model of the Bluetooth system is used as source of interference. Both modulation techniques are interesting for in-house communication due to the simpler frequency domain equalization.

articleTitle: Robust and scalable matching pursuits video transmission using the Bluetooth air interface standard
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper introduces an error resilient implementation of the matching pursuits algorithm for video coding. The video bitstream is transmitted using the simulated Bluetooth air interface standard, which recommends ARQ as a means of overcoming channel errors in data packets. This may be unsuitable for real time and broadcast applications. Therefore, a modified receiver is proposed in this paper, which does not request a retransmission of erroneous packets, but instead passes them to the video decoder to exploit error resilience. This strategy is shown to be superior to a standard compliant system if ARQ cannot be applied. This work confirms that wireless communication standards should support a transparent mode for video applications.

articleTitle: A next generation high capacity media for digital still cameras
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We developed iD (integrated, image disk) which is offered as a very suitable application format for digital still cameras. It has a high capacity of 730 MB, while being the world's smallest rewritable optical disk of 50 mm diameter.

articleTitle: An efficient digital image stabilizing technique for mobile video communications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this paper, we present a computationally efficient digital image stabilization (DIS) scheme for mobile video communications. Simulation results show that the proposed DIS technique with the K-means clustering algorithm can effectively estimate camera motion (hand-movement) using motion vectors decoded from a received video stream such as an MPEG sequence.

articleTitle: Speech synthesis software with variable speaking rate and its implementation on a 32-bit microprocessor
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We proposed a speech synthesis method with variable speaking rate based on phoneme duration features of natural speech. The real-time synthesis software required 8 MIPS CPU power was achieved on a 32-bit microprocessor.

articleTitle: A low-power MPEG audio layer III decoder IC with an integrated digital-to-analog converter
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: An MP3 decoder IC including a stereo DAC suitable for portable players is presented. The DAC uses digital interpolation to operate on a fixed output sample rate. The 28.5 mm/sup 2/ IC consumes 40-50 mW.

articleTitle: Architectural considerations for a digital set-top box with mass storage
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Adding a hard disk to a digital set-top box seems easy, but only if it roughly imitates today's analog systems. The new possibilities offered by time shifting in a digital receiver pose some interesting architectural problems.

articleTitle: Person adaptive autostereoscopic monitor (PAM)
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The PAM is an autostereoscopic monitor that presents three dimensional pictures and scenes to the user. It avoids moving glasses and can be added very easily to any computer system with a flat panel TFT display.

articleTitle: Architecture design of an MPEG-4 system
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: MPEG-4, the newest generation of MPEG compression standards is the first object-oriented coding standard in the world. It integrates scene and object descriptions into the bitstream to provide object reusability. From a technology point of view MPEG-4 includes coding objects of natural and synthetic content so that a wider spectrum of applications can be developed. With respect to media transmission, it communicates with networks via standardized interfaces, and therefore can adapt to a variety of network protocols. To design an architecture for a generic standard that covers broad areas, the designers should have a knowledge-base in various fields, so that the solution can be efficient and complete. We use Microsoft multimedia architecture, Directshow/sup TM/, to devise a total solution for MPEG-4 systems. Three major components (MPEG-4 server, player control and real-time encoder) are addressed; moreover, the modules required in each component and the corresponding functionality and mechanism are also discussed. The proposed architecture provides a useful framework for MPEG-4 software and hardware designers to follow.

articleTitle: Second generation DSP software for picture rate conversion
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Great progress has been made in motion estimation (ME). This has led to a high-quality second-generation scan-rate conversion (SRC) algorithm which runs on a commercially available programmable platform. The new system has a higher quality of motion estimation/compensation and de-interlacing than the first generation. The paper presents the new algorithm, and highlights the advances in performance.

articleTitle: Video analysis and classification for MPEG-7 applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Current information and communication technologies provide the infrastructure to send bits anywhere, but do not presume to handle information at the semantic level. Consequently, the huge amount of multimedia data imposes people a heavy burden of manipulating, including searching/choosing, interpreting, skimming, and integrating information. Thus automatic video content analysis, including video semantic category classification is necessary for various MPEG-7 applications, such as video content-based retrieval databases, on-line video indexing and filtering, video summaries for browsing systems and so on. We implemented and applied a set of simple visual/motional feature descriptors to our proposed video semantic category classification system for various applications.

articleTitle: Non-sequential video content representation using temporal variation of feature vectors
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient non-sequential representation of the video content is presented based on the temporal variation of the extracted feature trajectory. The proposed scheme is very fast and accurate and can be applied to any generic video stream. Many benefits in the field of image communication, storage requirements and efficient performance of indexing and retrieval algorithms can gain from such a non-linear representation.

articleTitle: System-on-a-chip for digital still cameras with VGA-size video clip shooting
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: An advanced, compact, and energy efficient system-on-a-chip has been developed that permits a single chip to perform all of the necessary functions for a DSC (digital still camera). Quality VGA-size motion pictures can be recorded at a rate of 30 fps (frames per second).

articleTitle: A flexible chipset architecture for client-side ADSL modems
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A new chipset architecture for client-side asymmetric digital subscriber line (ADSL) modems is presented. A general purpose DSP core coupled with a small number of dedicated peripheral circuits is used to implement the demodulation and decoding algorithms. A single highly integrated analog chip and a few passive components complete the analog portion of the modem. Programmability provides flexibility for adapting to changing standards and customer requirements, even with modems already deployed to the field. High levels of integration achieve the affordability required for massive consumer deployment.

articleTitle: A video indexing system using character recognition
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We design and implement a video indexing system. For automatic indexing of video images, character recognition information is utilized. The proposed system consists of three components: keyframe extraction, text extraction, and text recognition. It extracts text regions using a neural network that operates as a set of texture discrimination filters, and performing profile analysis with some heuristics. To ensure accurate segmentation of touching characters, character segmentation and recognition are performed in turn. The proposed system has been tested with 390 Korean news archives.

articleTitle: A shift-resisting blind watermark system for panoramic images
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The digital watermark is a technique used to protect the ownership of images and their associated software. A useful watermark scheme should be visually imperceptible and must be robust to resist various attacks: such as JPEG compression, pixel-shifting, cropping, blurring, etc. We propose a new watermarking technique that achieves the prescribed goals. We add synchronization bits to maintain the correct position information of the original 8/spl times/8 DCT block during the extracting phase. To avoid cropping some part of image and losing watermark information, we add watermark bits according to the edging features of each block. Therefore, the proposed approach needs neither the original image nor the original watermark pattern for watermark extraction, which is a useful feature in protecting real-time generated panorama images.

articleTitle: Home networking: a telecom's perspective
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper gives an overview of the home networking from a telecom operator and service provider's point of view. It gives an insight of the basic requirement of an integrated home network that can enable the delivery of advanced telecommunication services. Prerequisites of an enhanced public-to-private network interface (residential gateway) and results of a cooperative European project integrating heterogeneous home networks are reported.

articleTitle: Home network middleware architecture for supporting both dynamic reconfiguration and real-time services
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a middleware architecture for supporting dynamic reconfiguration and real-time services in home networks. The proposed home network middleware establishes a service channel between the application server and small consumer devices as well as accommodating the real-time requirements of home network services.

articleTitle: A study for the optical wireless module based on IEEE 1394
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We are currently developing a 125 Mbps optical wireless module for a proposed infrared-based IEEE 1394/S100 system. So as to avoid the affect of reflections, the module is implemented IEEE 1394 arbitration for a half-duplex optical link between the transmitter and receiver. One possibility is to develop a compact module for future use in handheld equipment.

articleTitle: Television meta-data standardization overview and opportunities
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of how data describing the content available on a television viewing system, hereafter called television meta-data or TV meta-data, can be generated, transported, and used independently of the actual content delivery. The first, and most widespread, use of TV meta-data is in support of electronic program guides (EPG), although other applications are beginning to appear. Standardization of the basic interchange formats, structure and content of meta-data collections is highly desirable, as it creates exciting opportunities in the creation, dissemination and use of this data.

articleTitle: Internet enabled digital photography
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The exposure of consumers to the Internet is opening up broad new markets for data-centric services and products. One of these new markets is that of digital photography. A key to growing this emerging market segment lies in simplifying the mechanisms for connecting digital cameras and other sources of digital images to the Internet. We describe a number of mechanisms of achieving such connectivity using existing desktop PC and Web technology, and additionally using a new generation of consumer Internet appliances. In addition details are given of the server-side infrastructure required to support a range of network-oriented services.

articleTitle: Fade, dissolve and wipe production in MPEG-2 compressed video
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: With the increase of digital technology in video production, several types of complex video special effects editing have begun to appear in video clips. In this paper, a novel algorithm is proposed for fade-in, fade-out, dissolve and wipe video editing operations in MPEG-2 compressed domain without full frame decompression and motion reestimation. The results show that both the objective and subjective quality of the edited video in the compressed domain closely follows the quality of the edited video in uncompressed video at the same bit rate.

articleTitle: Scalable and configurable software/hardware development for voice over packet networks
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of a scalable and configurable architecture on a voice over packet (VoP) network application consisting of an ensemble of signal processing components including a speech codec, and an echo canceller. Each of these components imposes different demands on processor resources and the processor engines can be configured to suit the needs of the application. This paper discusses system-on-chip (SoC) design methodology and the implementation of the VoP application and compares the performance of VoP components with various processor configurations.

articleTitle: Secure agent-mediated online auction framework
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper intends to apply software agent technology along with cryptographic technology to automate and secure online auction and presents a new secure agent-mediated online auction framework.

articleTitle: On the design and implementation of an MPEG-4 scene editor
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A prototype of MPEG-4 scene editor has been developed in the joint research of our laboratories and CyberLink Inc. With this scene editor, users can compose and edit object-oriented multimedia contents conforming to the MPEG-4 specification. The system is currently developed on Microsoft Windows platform. We describe the system architecture as well as the design and implementation issues of the scene editor. We believe our development experience can benefit future developers of the MPEG-4 system.

articleTitle: The design and implementation of TV tuner for digital terrestrial broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The DTV tuner for 8-VSB modulation was developed with satisfying the requirements of the ATSC. The double frequency conversion and the active tracking filter in the front-end were used for the cancellation of the interferences between adjacent channels and multi-channels by suppressing IF beat and image band. However, it was impossible to get frequency mapping between the tracking filter and the first VCO in the existing DTV tuner structure differing from the NTSC tuner. This paper, therefore, suggests the available structure and a new method for automatic frequency selection by obtaining the mapping of frequency characteristic over the tracking voltage and the combined hardware which is composed of a microcontroller, EEPROM, D/A, op amp and switch driver.

articleTitle: The contour shape descriptor for MPEG-7 and its applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a technical overview and performance evaluation of the contour shape descriptor adopted for the MPEG-7 experimental model. It also describes several examples of its application to new MPEG-7 compliant products.

articleTitle: A VLSI architecture for 2D mesh-based video object motion estimation
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel 2D mesh-based object motion estimation architecture that generates a content-based video object. The video object is represented using an alpha plane and a texture. The alpha plane consists of two layers (1) a mesh layer and (2) a binary layer that defines the object boundary. The texture defines the object's colors. The mesh layer is represented by a new adaptive hierarchical mesh. The proposed mesh is formed by recursive triangulation of the initial coarse mesh geometry, which reduces the mesh code. The proposed architecture generates a progressive mesh code. The proposed architecture offers low power performance at the algorithm level as follows: (1) decomposing the mesh into independent triangular patches that can be processed in parallel, (2) using a hierarchical structured triangulation technique, that simplify the processing unit, and (3) using the three steps motion estimation algorithm to simplify the motion estimation of the mesh nodes. The proposed architecture is suitable for very low bit rate online applications and it can be used as a building block for an MPEG-4 codec.

articleTitle: Frame rate up-conversion using the wavelet transform
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a new frame rate upconversion algorithm using the wavelet transform. In the proposed scheme, motion estimation is performed using the information in the wavelet-transformed subbands. In addition, an effective compensation method for the occlusion areas, called overcompensation, is presented. Computer simulation shows a higher performance of the proposed upconversion scheme than conventional methods.

articleTitle: High-resolution image using several sampling-phase shifted images-density doubling of single chip color CCD with pixel-shift technique
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a new method that allows reconstruction of a high-resolution image utilizing several sampling phase-shifted images. The proposed method allows pixel-shift of a color filtered CCD with channel-dependent sampling pattern, and doubles the resolution of obtained images.

articleTitle: Object-based human face detection
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose an object-based human face detection method. The proposed method consists of two steps: region segmentation and facial region detection. In region segmentation, the input image is segmented by a genetic algorithm into several initial regions. Then, to merge the regions forming an object, we use the spatial similarity between two regions because the regions forming an object share some common spatial characteristics. In facial region detection, the facial regions are identified from the results of the region segmentation step using a skin-color model. This approach can detect multiple faces of multi-views and small size in a complex background environment.

articleTitle: Interpolation using neural network for digital still cameras
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a color interpolation method for single-chip digital cameras using artificial neural networks. Single-chip digital cameras use a color filter array and an interpolation method in order to produce high quality color images from sparsely sampled images. Experiments show that the proposed interpolation algorithm based on neural networks provides a better performance than the conventional interpolation algorithms.

articleTitle: xDSL tutorial and standards update
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this tutorial we take a detailed look at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Study Group 15's G.99x series recommendations (G.lite, G.dmt, G.hs, etc.) that provide a set of worldwide xDSL standards for broadband Internet access. The most noteworthy specification of the group is the G.lite, "splitterless" ADSL, that allows a significantly easier installation that can be performed by consumers. New technologies in development by the ITU for VDSL, SHDSL, and home networking are also be reviewed. An understanding of the xDSL fundamentals will allow consumer unit manufacturers to exploit a new networked class of consumer equipment.

articleTitle: Retail set-top box architecture for digital cable network
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Since the introduction of cable television in the United States, networks have grown from one-way analog to the more modern hybrid-fiber coax (HFC) two-way digital broadband networks of today. Early analog systems were often stretched to reach distant neighborhoods resulting in poor signal quality. Upgrades to digital plant, the introduction of audio/video compression, and HFC distribution systems enable a robust two-way broadband network, which can deliver myriad new services with excellent quality. During this digital upgrade process, equipment used both at the headend and at consumer premises was proprietary in nature and non-interoperable. The cable industry soon realized the disadvantages of proprietary equipment and decided to change their systems to a standards-based open system. In this system, multiple vendors will be able to compete and consumer premises equipment (CPE) will be manufactured to be portable and to be sold at retail. With that goal in mind, the cable industry began an initiative, CableLabs' OpenCable project, with the primary objective to standardize CPE functionality and interfaces, in addition to related components and equipment used in the cable plant, where access control can be maintained by cable operators.

articleTitle: DOCSIS cable modem service overview
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The DOCSIS cable modem upstream channel is available to individual modems in dedicated time slots. The system provides transmit opportunities for modems physically dispersed over several miles. Synchronization, bandwidth requests, and signal control mechanisms are discussed.

articleTitle: A single chip phoneme based HMM speech recognition system for consumer applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes a phoneme based HMM speech recognition system for the use in localized and mobile consumer appliances. Unlike other systems this combined hardware/software approach does not need external components like memories etc.

articleTitle: Development of a 1394 bridge system based on P1394.1
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We developed a 1394 bus bridge system. This paper describes the implementation method of the 1394 bus bridge system. In order to implement characteristic functions of the bridge system, we divided new functions into hardware and software, and we examined hardware/software functions individually. Also, we developed a proprietary 1394 bus bridge system. This work makes it possible to realize 1394 bus bridge system that is compliant with P1394.1.

articleTitle: Validation experiments on structural, conceptual, collection, and access description schemes for MPEG-7
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have contributed to the development and validation of several description schemes for multimedia content, which have been integrated into the emerging MPEG-7 standard. This paper includes summaries of the validation experiments of these description schemes.

articleTitle: Implementation of H.323 multipoint video conference systems with personal presence control
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents an H.323 standard compliant video conference system architecture. Both the server side and client side implementations are addressed. Video processing for advanced personal presence features including dynamic rate allocation and video object manipulation are also presented.

articleTitle: Development of VSB demodulator LSI with high-performance waveform equalizer
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have newly developed a single chip VSB (vestigial side band) demodulator LSI for the US terrestrial digital TV system. In this LSI, we have improved the waveform equalization performance and reduced cost and power consumption by adopting an all-digital architecture and a waveform equalizer that uses a newly developed algorithm.

articleTitle: Progress in motion estimation for consumer video format conversion
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: There are now two generations of ICs for motion-compensated video format conversion (MC-VFC). Real-time DSP software for MC-VFC has previously been demonstrated, with the breakthroughs enabling this progress coming from motion estimation. The paper gives an overview.

articleTitle: A simple detection method for high-density d=1 optical recording
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a new bit-detection method which is applicable to high-density, d=1 optical recording systems. The new method combines the advantages of computational simplicity, non-recursive operations, as well as performance which approaches that of maximum likelihood sequence detection (MLSD), even at very high recording densities.

articleTitle: Iterative equalization-detection algorithm using trellis-based equalizer and RSC code for high density optical recording systems
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper proposes an iterative equalization and detection algorithm using trellis-based equalizer and recursive systematic convolutional (RSC) code for high density optical recording systems. The complexity of conventional detection schemes like PRML must be increased as the density is increased, but the proposed algorithm stays at the same complexity even though the density is increased. Furthermore, it does not employ modulation code.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of AAC decoders
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The MPEG-2 AAC (advanced audio coder) is a high-quality perceptual audio coder with flexible configurations enabling its use in many applications where high audio quality and limited transmission channel bandwidth are required. This paper provides a technology overview and describes the design and implementation of AAC decoders.

articleTitle: A preliminary report on the phase-I ATSC field test results in Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In May 1998, Taiwan formally adopted the ATSC digital television (DTV) as its local digital terrestrial broadcasting standard. In order to define the DTV service area and specify the transmission parameters, we like to know the characteristics of the DTV signal over the local irregular terrain, the impact of interference, and the relationship between the signal power and video quality. We measured the DTV signal and compared the DTV and the NTSC service availability. We selected 100 test sites in Taipei city and its vicinity including three types of environment: urban, suburban and rural areas. In general, the DTV system has a clear advantage over the NTSC system in reception quality.

articleTitle: Reduction of blocking artifacts in MPEG-2 video using a block classification technique
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method to remove blocking artifacts for application to MPEG-2 video. In this method, coding information such as DCT coefficients and motion vectors is utilized to classify each block. Blocking artifacts are detected by using the classification results and removed with spatial filtering. The effectiveness of this method has been verified through computer simulation.

articleTitle: A camera chipset for dual-mode mega-pixel camcorders
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have developed a dual mode camera system chipset for camcorders which provides high quality image in both movie mode and still mode. The system employs 1.07 Mega pixel CCD, a DSP with a real-time image resolution converter, and a 33 MHz analog front-end processor. With this chipset we achieved over 500 TV-line resolution in the movie mode and an improved interface between still/movie image formats.

articleTitle: Single integrated DSP with TBC for cameras/recorders
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have developed a single chip DSP (digital signal processor) for cameras/recorders with low cost and high picture quality. We realized an internal TBC (time base corrector) essential for outputting a digital picture signal recorded on a tape as an analog format. This DSP also features the digital interface based on ITU-R BT.656.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of Bluetooth systems in the presence of AWGN, fading, multipaths, and inband interference
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper analyzes the effects of interference on the performance of a Bluetooth system. The analysis is based on the simulation results from the baseband model of the system.

articleTitle: Digital Music in the 21st Century
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper will overview the MPEG4 and MPEG7 standards for music and digital audio, especially the Structured Audio approach to synthetic music compression and the use of audio metadata under MPEG7.

articleTitle: A printed circuit switched array antenna for indoor communications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a new printed switched array antenna suitable for low-cost indoor communications. The antenna uses printed antenna elements having minimal mutual coupling effects and it may produce either omni-directional or multi-directional overlapping patterns.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of error control algorithms for Bluetooth system: open-loop and closed-loop algorithms
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose open-loop and closed-loop link quality control (LQC) algorithms using the correlation output of the access code for a short-range radio network. The new schemes can decrease the number of retransmissions and data overhead which result in improving the throughput of the Bluetooth system without extra hardware burden.

articleTitle: A new indexing method for video retrieval using the rosette pattern
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a new method to index an image by using the rosette pattern. Our method is better than the conventional ones in terms of the reduction of the number of pixels required to index an image and also provides a good retrieval performance.

articleTitle: Regularized dequantizer for MPEG
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a new dequantization scheme based on regularization principles. The new approach drastically reduces blocking artifacts without smoothing the decoded image. The performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated against the standard MPEG decompression.

articleTitle: VLSI design of an efficient embedded zerotree wavelet coder with function of digital watermarking
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A hardware architecture is presented for the embedded zerotree wavelet (EZW) algorithm. We encode independently the symbols generated in the significant mapping (SMAP) and those in the successive approximation quantization (SAQ). Compared to previously proposed architectures, our design leads to fewer transmitted bits and thus alleviates the communication overhead without sacrificing PSNR.

articleTitle: Improvised assembly mechanism for VNA applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper proposes an improvised assembly mechanism (IAM), a novel mechanism for constructing virtual network appliances (VNA). IAM enables the automatic assembly of VNA with distributed functional components in a component-initiated and ad-hoc manner.

articleTitle: Hybrid compression of video with graphics in DVT communication systems
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A new cost-effective and "near-lossless" quality compression system for images containing both video and graphics is presented. The scheme can be used successfully in two distinct architectures: for professional video distribution from content provider to broadcaster, and for local memory reduction in a consumer DTV receiver.

articleTitle: A real-time IMT-2000 audio transmission system
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have a real-time audio transmission system designed for the ITM-2000 network. This system uses a real-time DSP encoder and decoder based on error-protected TwinVQ, and can transmit high-quality audio through the IMT-2000 network.

articleTitle: Integrated circuit system solutions for multi-standard digital TV receivers
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A concept for the simplification of tuner architectures for digital and analog TV is presented that supports solid state integration and is based on down conversion of UHF to baseband by means of a compensated mixer architecture. I/Q imbalance impairments can be removed in the analog and the digital part of the receiver.

articleTitle: A fast tagged sorter used in 100/10 Mbps routers
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a very fast circuit for a tagged sorter which has been integrated in 100/10 Mbps routers to resolve the re-ordering problem of incoming packets. The utilization of both edges of the clock is presented, which can drastically improve the clock speed and the throughput.

articleTitle: A low power full accuracy MPEG1 audio layer III (MP3) decoder with on-chip data converters
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A low power full accuracy MPEG1 audio layer 3 (MP3) decoder with on-chip data converters is proposed. The chip is composed of a digital block to implement MP3 decoding and voice compression/decompression algorithm, 12-bit recycling type A/D converter, and an oversampling /spl Delta//spl Sigma/ 1-bit D/A converter. An efficient power management technique is implemented to reduce power consumption for portable applications. The proposed decoder has been fabricated with a 4 metal 0.35 /spl mu/m CMOS technology and the chip area is about 6.4/spl times/6.7 mm/sup 2/ with 165 mW power dissipation at 2.7 V power supply.

articleTitle: A high speed Viterbi decoder using path limited PRML method and its application to 1/2 inch HD full bit rate digital VCR
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A new algorithm called "path limited PRML" is described which has been used to implement a high speed Viterbi decoder LSI. Furthermore, this LSI has been used to realize an experimental 1/2" DVCR at 1.3 Gbps.

articleTitle: Performance of OFDM carrier and sampling frequency synchronization on stationary and mobile channels
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: All-digital automatic frequency control (AFC) for consumer applications must be both simple and effective in all kinds of environments. This paper presents the AFC synchronization strategy adopted for a COFDM receiver chip previously developed and gives results on the tracking performance in both stationary and mobile environments.

articleTitle: The use of video sample rate converters to achieve three-dimensional effects
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a method of performing high-quality video scaling and advanced video juggling to achieve 3D video effects. This method does not rely on an expensive 3D graphics rendering unit but smartly combines simple geometric and perspective transformations with advanced video scaling. The key is to start from 2D video scaling, instead of graphics accelerators, for these 3D effects. Results show that the picture quality using this method greatly exceeds that with state-of-the-art 3D graphics rendering units. Furthermore, the complexity is only in the order of video sample rate converters (SRCs), which are usually already part of a high-end TV set.

articleTitle: MPEG audio video decoder with 2D graphic engine for HDTV
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes an audio video decoder for digital TV, digital set top box, and cable box. It contains an integrated, high performance 2D graphic engine and several display processors. The video decoder is a MP@HL decoder, which supports all ATSC/Grand Alliance standard formats. It can decode from several digital or analog sources, and the PIP feature is supported from any source. The audio decoder is an MPEG 1, 2, AC3 6 channels decoder with PCM overlay support. A standard definition display output is provided in parallel with the main display output, giving an auxiliary VCR output.

articleTitle: Card-sized portable audio player using high quality audio coding technology TwinVQ
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents an audio player using TwinVQ, an advanced high quality coding technology, which can compress 44.1 kHz sampled audio data at a very low bit rate of 40 kbit/s/ch. The player is business-card-sized of 10 mm thickness, and has practical performance with low power consumption.

articleTitle: Versatile single-chip digital TV encoder based on programmable hardware (CPLD)
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper discusses the synergy effects, which can be used to design a versatile multistandard digital television encoder with minimum hardware requirements. The paper shows the implementation possibilities of the signal-processing algorithms, which are used by modern broadband applications, in complex programmable logic devices (CPLDs). This is done by the example of a highly integrated digital TV encoder, which has been developed at the Chair of Communications Technology for measurement purposes. The low-chip-count solution is capable of encoding and modulating for satellite, cable and terrestrial transmission according to the European Digital Video Broadcasting Standards (DVB).

articleTitle: 3D geometry graphics system using deferred primitive rendering with VLIW geometry processor
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The geometry stage which performs the transformation and lighting operations of vertices, has become the critical part in the 3D graphics pipeline. We have designed the FGA (FLOVA Geometry Accelerator) that is the 3D geometry graphics system and it almost removes the time required for the process geometry stage. The 3D graphics library, FGA-GL, supports the FGA system. The deferred primitive rendering algorithm of FGA-GL enables the geometry processing of the primitive data to be done concurrently with the host job such as primitive data management or game AI. FGA improves the average performance of the 3D graphics system by 2.5-3.0 times.

articleTitle: A single-chip MP@HL HDTV decoder with integrated audio decoding and display processing units
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A single-chip MP@HL HDTV decoder that integrates all the functions of HDTV such as system parsing, audio decoding, video decoding and display processing is presented. By employing a programmable system parsing unit, the decoder can be applied to not only ATSC receivers but also DVB receivers or DVD players. All 18 ATSC format videos can be decoded and displayed on HD monitors or PC VGA monitors. The decoder also features arbitrary resolution conversion and powerful de-interlacing.

articleTitle: BDTE MRG-TCP extension for minimum rate guarantees with the integrated services on the Internet
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: BDTE MRG (bulk data transfer extension for minimum rate guarantee) is a TCP extension to guarantee a minimum transfer rate with the integrated services on the Internet. It divides one TCP stream into two flows to use the reserved channel and the common best effort channel simultaneously. BDTE MRG can get extra bandwidth without violating the minimum guaranteed rate so that it applies two different flow/congestion control schemes to each flow.

articleTitle: High efficiency optical system design for a liquid crystal projector
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a high efficiency optical system for a liquid crystal projector. The F number of the illumination system with or without a micro lens array on LCD panels, and color separation system has been optimized and the system provides a bright and high quality image.

articleTitle: System-on-silicon for 100 Hz TV: new concepts qualified for highest integration
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents the next generation of a low cost, high performance single-chip upconverter solution for flicker-free TV. This chip has been designed in a 0.18 /spl mu/m copper eDRAM technology. All processing stages between tuner output (CVBS) and RGB processor input are now integrated, requiring only a few external components. Applying a newly developed digital clock concept all clocks both of locked and unlocked types are derived from the same source. This increases flexibility and reliability by saving analog PLLs. The authors also describe the data processing with respect to the new concept.

articleTitle: Pitch alteration technique in a speech synthesis system
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper proposes the pitch alteration method that solves the energy unbalance by the pitch interval adjustment on a speech synthesis system. The pitch alteration is applied to waveform reconstruction and PSOLA (pitch synchronous overlap and add) techniques.

articleTitle: Video camera recorder using small-size DVD-RAM
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have developed a video camera recording using small-size 80 mm DVD-RAM with the following features: quick search, no accidental overwrite, high-quality picture for a long time, playback on PCs with a 4.7 GB DVD-RAM drive and future DVD players.

articleTitle: A multi-format transport demultiplexer for ARIB, ATSC, DSS and DVB formats
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We developed a multi-format transport stream demultiplexer that accepts ARIB, ATSC, DSS, and DVB formatted digital television broadcasts. To reduce host processor loading, it also features a unique "mismatch" section filtering function.

articleTitle: Video motion representation for improved content access
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes techniques for representing motion information in the context of multimedia description interfaces (being standardized by MPEG-7). Focusing on camera motion and object trajectories, it shows how such descriptions can help consumers to browse and query through large audio-visual connections.

articleTitle: A compact silicon microdisplay for virtual reality applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have developed a highly integrated liquid-crystal-on-silicon microdisplay for virtual reality applications. The silicon panel of 704/spl times/576 spatial resolution was designed and fabricated by a custom 0.35 /spl mu/m CMOS technology. The pixel pitch was 9.6 /spl mu/m and the fill factor was 88%. A three-dimensional (3D) video stream in an interlaced format was generated by a 3D modeling code for test and demonstration.
