A color sequential technique and control logic was implemented to obtain full color and extract video frames for the display. With two silicon microdisplays and eyepieces for each eye, we have demonstrated a 3D stereoscopic display.

articleTitle: Distributed family wallet architecture and secure inter-purse operations
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a new electronic wallet concept called distributed family wallet (DFW). More than classical operations allowed by current e-wallets, DFW provides inter-purse operations allowing digital tokens to be securely transferred between several purses in the family environment.

articleTitle: The bit rate of reality [picture/sound reproduction]
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: After years of work in film and television the author attended a professional basketball game. He found there that the live experience was much different from the recorded ones with which he had been working. Comparing the frequency, amplitude, and spatial domains of sound, and the corresponding ones for picture, between real and recorded events led him to calculate how many bits would be needed per second to make a reproduction essentially identical to the real thing.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of warping filters inside car cockpits
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Sound reproduction within a car inside is a difficult task. Reverberation, reflection, echo, noise and vibration are some of the issues to account for. A first step in the direction of increasing sound comfort is that of equalizing the acoustic pressure response in the frequency domain. A direct solution is that of implementing with a convolution filter the inverse of the acoustic measurements in the car cockpit. However this often results in very high number of taps, therefore more complex techniques must be adopted, which rely also on psychoacoustic considerations. An automatic tools to develop warping inverse filters for target car cockpits was designed and validated through experiments in commercial cars.

articleTitle: High density optical disk system using D8-15 modulation code and new signal-processing techniques
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A new 8-15 RLL(2,10) modulation code and a new 2D adaptive equalizer are combined with a 0.7 NA objective lens and a violet LD. Bit error rates are measured with a 19.8 GB ROM disk.

articleTitle: Timing-offset independent equalization techniques for robust indoor reception of ATSC DTV receivers
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a fractionally-spaced decision feedback equalizer with stop-and-go algorithm for robust indoor reception of ATSC DTV receivers. The fractionally-spaced decision feedback equalizer outperforms the conventional decision feedback equalizer in the area of short delay echoes, which can generate large symbol timing offsets.

articleTitle: Motion vector recovery using optical flow
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A compressed bitstream generated by an MPEG-2 video coder is sensitive to channel errors. Due to the coding structure of the MPEG-2 video compression algorithm, a bit error can affect not only the current picture frame but also succeeding frames. In this paper, we propose a temporal error concealment algorithm to recover lost or erroneously received motion vectors. In order to estimate the motion vector of the erroneous macroblock at the decoder we use the average value of optical flow vectors of neighboring luminance intensity values.

articleTitle: Computer simulation tools for the design and optimization of optical disk systems
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes the development and application of software models for the design and optimization of the record, readout and data recovery processes in all commonly used optical disk storage formats.

articleTitle: The multimedia home goes mobile
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: It is widely accepted today that the multimedia terminal in the home will serve a different purpose than a desktop PC. Many committees and companies are currently trying to define the open application platform for tomorrow's consumer terminals for home use, among others is the so-called multimedia home platform (MHP) of the European DVB project. Meanwhile, consumers and the car industry are getting interested in mobile access to multimedia services. This paper summarizes the trends and opportunities of mobile multimedia, especially in the DVB domain.

articleTitle: Scalable video decoder and its application to multi-channel multicast system
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this paper, we propose scalable video decoder algorithms using several DCT manipulations such as low pass filtering and resolution conversion in the DCT domain, and their application to a multi-channel multicast system. In the experiment, it has been shown that simultaneous decoding of tens of channels in an ordinary PC can be realized by selecting an appropriate decoding scheme.

articleTitle: Shape adaptive padding for MPEG-4
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In MPEG-4 video object coding, the boundary blocks of reference video objects are padded by replicating the boundary samples towards the exterior. In this paper we propose a novel shape distortion adaptive hybrid padding technique to minimise prediction errors and improve compression efficiency. We show that this technique results in boundary block coding gains of up to 9% as compared to that of the MPEG-4 scheme.

articleTitle: MLP decoder for DVD-Audio player
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: There are two audio decoding formats defined by the DVD-Audio specification 1.0. These formats are uncompressed LPCM and compressed PPCM (packed PCM). Meridien Lossless Packing (MLP) has been adopted by the DVD consortium as the standard PPCM compressed format. All DVD-Audio players must support this format. Consumer electronic manufacturers are designing and developing both DVD-Audio players as well as combined DVD-Video/DVD-Audio players (also called Universal players). This paper provides an overview of a DVD-Audio implementation (including MLP), added system features, and design tradeoffs for a Universal DVD player.

articleTitle: Improvement of the positioning accuracy of a software-based GPS receiver using a 32-bit embedded microprocessor
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The improvement of the positioning accuracy of a software-based GPS receiver using a 32-bit embedded microprocessor is proposed. The positioning error is reduced from 37.2 m to 1.9 m by using the DGPS function and Kalman filter.

articleTitle: A TV drama digesting method based on the mental side of the content
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: In this study, a method to digest a TV drama based on the mental side of the picture content is proposed and implemented. The video structure model which consists of the tracks of an actor's utterances, BGM, offset noise, effect sounds and video shots is defined and the relation between the chosen frames in the digest and their structural features in a live drama video and the broadcast digest made by the professional beforehand is clarified. The system, which implements the relation, determines the candidate frames for the digest of the video based on the relation information and makes a digest of the specified length.

articleTitle: Robust image transmission over CDMA channels
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We present our study of wireless image transmission over a CDMA link. To deal with the limited bandwidth problem of the wireless channel, we implement packetized zerotree wavelet (PWZ) coding scheme. For the error prone problem, we utilized the cyclic redundancy code (CRC) of CDMA links.

articleTitle: An MPEG-4 object-based transcoder: architecture and applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The architecture of an MPEG-4 based transcoder is presented. We discuss new algorithms to select the quantization parameter for every object and introduce some new applications for Internet and wireless communications.

articleTitle: Electronic music distribution (EMD) creates new consumer devices
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The history and state of the art of audio coding technology (like MP3 or AAC) is presented. Available solutions for electronic music distribution (EMD) systems are summarized with a focus on the prevention of piracy and on SDMI (Secure Digital Music Initiative) compliant applications.

articleTitle: Design, implementation and field trial of terrestrial digital television system in Korea
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents design, implementation and field trial of terrestrial DTV (digital television) system made in ETRI, Korea. The DTV system is ATSC compliant and under field trial in Korea.

articleTitle: An efficient loop/post filter to reduce annoying artifacts of H.26L video coder
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: An efficient two-dimensional loop and post filter is addressed to reduce blocking and ringing artifacts of H.26L compressed video. A new two-dimensional regularized smoothing functional is defined and the regularization parameters controlling the degree of smoothness to four neighboring directions are determined by available information. Therefore, no information is necessary to obtain the recovered image from the compressed video. The experimental results show the capability of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: 8-VSB channel coding analysis for DTV broadcast
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This article analyzes the channel coding stage in 8-VSB (8-level vestigial sideband) transmission for DTV (digital television) broadcast, proposed by ATSC (Advanced Television Systems Committee). We present BER (bit error rate) results for a codec simulator developed by the authors for the purpose of assessing the robustness of the ATSC 8-VSB coding stage in presence of an additive Gaussian noise channel and of impulsive channel noise surges. We discuss implementation aspects for the developed simulator.

articleTitle: Fast object tracking in digital video
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a fast semi-automatic semantic object tracking algorithm for digital video. The proposed method consists of two steps, namely, intra-frame object extraction and the inter-frame object tracking. For the intra-frame segmentation, we try to minimize the human intervention by exploiting the automatic homogenous region segmentation. Then, to achieve a fast inter-frame object tracking, we propose to use 1-D projected motion estimation and an improved flooding method for the watershed algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of real-time image enhancement preprocessor for CMOS image sensor
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a design of the real time digital image enhancement preprocessor for CMOS image sensor. The CMOS image sensor offers various advantages while it provides lower-quality images than CCD does. In order to compensate for the physical limitation of CMOS sensor the spatially adaptive contrast enhancement algorithm was incorporated into the preprocessor with color interpolation, gamma correction, and automatic exposure control. The efficient hardware architecture for the preprocessor is proposed and was simulated in VHDL. It is composed of about 19 K logic gates, which is suitable for low-cost one-chip PC camera. The test system was implemented on FPGA chip in real-time mode, and performed successfully.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a computationally efficient TEQ for DMT-based xDSL modem
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper is concerned with a new algorithm which can be used to design a time-domain equalizer (TEQ) for xDSL systems employing discrete multitone (DMT) modulation. The proposed algorithm, derived by neglecting the terms which do not affect the performance of a DMT system in ARMA modeling, is shown to have a good performance compared with the previous TEQ algorithms even with a significantly lower computational complexity.

articleTitle: Adaptive timing synchronization scheme for a short-ranged Bluetooth network
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes an adaptive timing synchronization scheme of a short-ranged Bluetooth system in the partial-band noise environments. The variance of the partial-band interference is estimated and is utilized for the trigger threshold value of the inquiry scan and page scan states. Numerical results show the proposed synchronization algorithm is robust to the partial-band noise interference.

articleTitle: Multi-agent architecture for intelligent home network service using tuple space model
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The major design challenge to realize intelligent home network services is organizing distributed and heterogeneous home devices effectively. In order to meet the design challenge, an agent space based multi-agent architecture is considered. In addition, we also proposed a new middleware on the IEEE1394 network to support reliable communication between agent spaces.

articleTitle: MPEG-2 AAC decoder for a 32-bit MCU
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: New implementation techniques for MPEG-2 AAC software by using a 32-bit general-purpose MCU and DRAM are proposed. These make it possible to realize real-time decoding on an evaluation board.

articleTitle: Priority queue-based IEEE 1394 device driver for supporting real-time characteristics
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper proposes an architecture of IEEE 1394 device driver that support the priority-based queueing of packets for guaranteeing real-time characteristics, and improve the predictability of high priority application. This architecture can accommodate the real-time requirements of various applications and devices that include digital multimedia equipment with QoS guarantee and real-time middleware for implementing the IEEE 1394 based home network.

articleTitle: Advanced modulation schemes for cable TV upstream channel
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper addresses the topic of the reverse channel in cable TV networks-maximizing the capabilities of the upstream spectrum using advanced modulation and demodulation techniques. We provide an overview of the different modulation schemes that were proposed for the next generation cable modem upstream physical layer (also known as 'HI PHY') in the IEEE 802.14 standardization committee and describe the solution that was finally chosen by the leading silicon vendors in the cable modem industry.

articleTitle: Home server with multi-channel recording capability
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We developed a home video server with multi-channel recording capability. It filters/stores up to 3 different audio-video broadcast streams simultaneously, while playing-back another stream from disk media in either normal- or trick-mode. The server is shown to provide viewers with simple user-interface for recording and replaying broadcast programs.

articleTitle: IC for phone line home networking
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes the 10 Mbps phone line home networking IC that allows consumer electronic devices such as audio players, personal computers and IP telephones to be easily and cost effectively networked in a typical home environment using the existing household phone line wires and RJ-11 phonejacks. The IC implements an industry specification developed to allow concurrent network usage with normal analog phone service and asymmetric digital subscriber line (ADSL) on the same pair of wires. Additionally, the IC divides the different types of traffic (voice, audio, video, Internet) into different classes of service so that important or time sensitive traffic can be given a quality of service (QoS) guarantee. The challenges associated with varieties of unstructured household phone wiring are described and how they are overcome with the application of equalization techniques.

articleTitle: Development of a bi-directional remote controller protocol and systems for domestic appliances
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The authors have proposed the BCP protocol that enables remote controllers to communicate compatibly with all equipment regardless of manufacturers. We have also developed the platform of universal controllers and the UC adapters for domestic appliances based on proposed BCP/ECP specifications. This combination allowed for full interoperability in the integrated model system featuring UCs with bi-directional communication, as expected.

articleTitle: Design and implement an interface on PDA for Korean
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We present an interface on the personal digital assistant (PDA) that recognize Korean characters. The interface applies a path discriminant hidden Markov model (PDHMM) for Korean characters. The PDHMM is available for the cursive type of Korean characters.

articleTitle: Approach to a higher data transfer rate in 15-Gb DWDD-MO recording
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have studied high-density MO (magneto-optical) recording using a DWDD (domain wall displacement detection) medium with a red diode laser and a 0.60-NA objective lens. Using the same optical parameters of a DVD (digital versatile disc) system, we obtained an acceptable bit error rate of 4.8/spl times/10/sup -4/ with an areal density of 11 Gbit/in/sup 2/ and a data-transfer rate of 20 Mbit/sec. In addition, we analyzed the noise components to achieve much higher transfer-rate recording.

articleTitle: The robustness verification for the D-VHS trick play using dynamic measurement method for evaluating mechanism
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have developed a new method for evaluating the trick play mechanism. It enables defining ideal distribution for D-VHS trick play data on the tape. An ideal balance of both mechanism accuracy and data distribution facilitates mass production.

articleTitle: Complexity evaluation for the implementation of a pre-FFT equalizer in an OFDM receiver
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A pre-FFT equalizer (PFE) has been shown to offer a significant throughput efficiency improvement when applied to an OFDM receiver. The required computational complexity to implement such an equalizer is evaluated assuming the LMS adaptation algorithm. The paper concludes by discussing the potential efficiency and complexity trade-offs that can be achieved when applying this technology to standards such as Hiperlan/2, IEEE P802.11a and DVB-T.

articleTitle: Software design of a personal television service
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Personal television service (PTS) software must be deployed on a broad variety of set-top boxes, operating systems, middleware and network types. This paper presents a PTS architecture with special attention to these topics.

articleTitle: A cost effective architecture for HDTV with 2D/3D graphics
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: An integrated MPEG-2 transport demultiplexer and MP@HL video decoder and 2D/3D graphics core are presented. The described architecture integrates all digital decoding and graphics functions into one system, analog video encoding and decoding functions into other system and digital teletext/subtitling decoding functions and user or private data processing on a midrange performance host CPU (Pentium 200 MHz or MIPS 166 MHz). This results in the greater flexibility and reduction of hardware cost of digital set-top receivers.

articleTitle: Hybrid audio coding for speech and audio below medium bit rate
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A novel a audio/speech coding algorithm, hybrid audio coding (HAC) is described. New features of the algorithm include window switching with generalized MDCT, an improved quantization scheme of the MDCT coefficients, and waveform normalization in the time domain. HAC provides a good quality at a bit rate of 8 to 16 kbps, and it is also proven that the developed algorithm is effective for both audio and speech signals.

articleTitle: Portal directory broadcast system
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: dbsThis paper proposes the first prototype implemented with the broad based directory service systems characterized by synchronization protocol data unit filtering. The system improves retrieval capability for contents delivery systems under minimum resource constraints.

articleTitle: A wide range PLL for 64X speed CD-ROM & 10X speed DVD-ROM
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose a wide range PLL (phase locked loop) for 64X speed CD-ROM and 10X speed DVD-ROM. The proposed PLL has a locking range of 75 MHz-370 MHz. A new V-I converter and a differential delay cell are used in a 3-stage ring VCO to reduce jitter. In addition, we propose a new charge pump which has perfect current matching characteristics for sourcing/sinking currents. This new charge pump improves the locking time and the locking range of the PLL. Implemented in a 0.25 /spl mu/m, 1-poly 5-metal CMOS process, the wide range PLL consumes less than 100 mW with a single 2.5 V power supply. It occupies an active area of 1.9 mm by 1.1 mm.

articleTitle: OFDM system with the guard interval and the one-tap equalizer bank for the wireless-LAN
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We propose an OFDM system with the guard interval and the simple one-tap equalizer bank under the two-ray multipath channel for the wireless-LAN. The simple one-tap equalizer bank is necessary to support the required BER, 10/sup -5/ under the two-ray multipath channel with the mean of the second-ray's attenuation coefficient, E[/spl alpha/]=0.25, and the normalized frequency offset, which is normalized about the subcarrier tone spacing, /spl Delta/fTs/spl les/10%.

articleTitle: MPEG-2 video decompression on a multiprocessing VLIW microprocessor
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The compression and decompression of MPEG-2 video play a major role in entertainment delivery devices. This paper investigates software MPEG-2 video decoding on a multiprocessing microprocessor, MAJC-5200. MAJC (microprocessor architecture for Java computing), is a very long instruction word (VLIW) processor with an instruction set geared towards multimedia computing. We describe the microprocessor and show that less than 50% of a single CPU out of the available true processors is sufficient for decoding 4 Mb/s video sequences.

articleTitle: MPEG-7 standard and its expected role in development of new information appliances
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: MPEG-7 is a new standardization activity for standardizing descriptions of audiovisual information and user preferences. Descriptions can be utilized for filtering, searching, and navigation of audiovisual information as well as personalization of consumption of audiovisual information.

articleTitle: Loop prevention for IEEE 1394 network
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The loop prevention method, which avoids misconnection (loop connection) and realizes a reliable network is proposed. The port disable function of P1394a is applied to the IEEE 1394 network. The restoration time is experimentally obtained to be around 1.4 msec for a network including 3 loops.

articleTitle: Some elementary suboptimal diversity reception schemes for DVB-T in mobile conditions
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Some simple diversity reception schemes are presented to be used with DVB-T systems in multipath channels with time selective fading. The performances of these methods are examined using simulation. The results show, that even very simple diversity selection strategies can improve the system performance considerably.

articleTitle: Integrated Home Service Network on Intelligent Intranet
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: The IHSNII (Integrated Home Service Network on Intelligent Intranet) is a Web-based home service system. It can provide omnibus security services including ISP (Internet service provider), household appliances control service, medical service, automatic meter reading service, home security services, etc. IHSNII is developed to integrate different HSASS (home service application supporting system) and provide a uniform GUI (graphic user interface) for the end user by using a Web browser. In addition, XML (extensible markup language) is used to describe data and specify interchange formats.

articleTitle: Trust-worthy video enforcement for electronic toll collection
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A verification mechanism of vehicle images based on digital watermarking is proposed. This mechanism can be used to detect the modification on watermarked vehicle images. In addition, the modified pixels can also be pointed out by this verification mechanism. It can therefore make the video enforcement of the ETC (electronic toll collection) trust-worthy.

articleTitle: Computation-effective 3-D graphics rendering architecture for embedded multimedia system
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A new architecture is proposed to realize 3-D graphics rendering for an embedded multimedia system. Because only 20% to 83% triangles in original 3-D object models are visible by simulation, our architecture is designed to eliminate the redundant operations on invisible triangles without image quality loss. The simulation and analysis results shows that this architecture can save 5% to 60.3% CPU operations compared with traditional architectures.

articleTitle: Input processing IC for NTSC and ATSC signals
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes a mixed-signal IC for receiving both NTSC and ATSC signals. The signals enter the IC in the analog domain (IF or baseband) and are digitized in a 'switch box'. They are then output as separate digital video and audio. The IC is controlled across an I/sup 2/C-bus link.

articleTitle: Flexible solutions for low-level visual feature descriptors in MPEG-7
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper reports descriptors for basic visual information features (color, texture, shape, motion) developed in the context of the forthcoming MPEG-7 standard. Modular and flexible solutions are presented, which allow a wide range of possible applications.

articleTitle: High quality multi-scan converter for XGA-LCD projector by video DSP
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-scan converter for the XGA-LCD projector using video DSP that an handle 140 (70/spl times/2) MHz peak I/O signals. Applying video DSP, the proposed system realizes high quality conversion and multi-functions for various formats. It also remarkably reduces the development term and manpower.

articleTitle: Agent-mediated Internet advertising models
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper intends to apply software agents to automate Internet advertising and presents four models of agent-mediated Internet advertising: negotiation and payment, push, post and pull models.

articleTitle: Enabling video processing in wireless terminals with a new open multimedia application platform
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: To enable video applications in wireless mobile phones, Texas Instruments (TI) introduces a new open multimedia application platform. This platform will deliver the advanced processing required to make video functions a reality, without compromising the power efficiency essential to wireless communications devices. The paper describes the open multimedia application platform architecture, emphasizing its strength for video applications. The DSP core used in this platform is then detailed, with a special focus on new instructions provided by this new processor, which are especially suited to improve video processing algorithm execution.

articleTitle: Tuning system for low voltage zero-IF digital satellite receivers
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: A new tuning system is described that reduces the phase noise of fully integrated, low tuning voltage VCOs. Zero-IF receivers employing this tuning system architecture do not suffer from typical zero-IF problems. It enables a better RF performance, a robust receiver design and an easier RF application.

articleTitle: Elements of a baseline definition of cable/consumer electronics compatibility for digital television
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Minimum requirements have been developed for cable television systems and digital television receivers so that the receiver may be connected directly to the RF output of the cable system to provide the following baseline service: in-the-clear NTSC analog and DTV programs; scrambled DTV programs using a POD module (including PPV and subscription programs ordered by phone; and event information data). The technical elements of this baseline definition are presented as well as the related standards development activities and any FCC decisions in this field.

articleTitle: Audio processing on AV decoder LSI for DVD-audio
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We have developed an AV (audio and video) decoder LSI for both DVD-audio and DVD-video standard. We describe the architecture of the LSI and the audio software algorithms for real-time decoding of high quality audio contents (192 Hz 24 bit stereo, 96 kHz 24 bit multi-channel, etc.) with still picture.

articleTitle: A description scheme for video based on feature extraction in the compressed domain
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Feature extraction in the compressed domain enables fast but somewhat inaccurate computation. We describe a video description scheme that makes use of a combination of features extracted in the compressed domain so as to compensative for the lack of accuracy of each individual extraction.

articleTitle: Designing low-cost digital BTSC stereo encoders for consumer video source equipment
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper introduces technical details for a low-cost digital BTSC compatible encoder implementation for consumer equipment. The paper presents the reciprocal index lookup table technique, a key enabling technology for efficient logic implementation of the variable spectral compressor, and presents a tutorial on the design of gate-efficient audio filters in digital logic.

articleTitle: 22 GB optical disc system for high definition digital video recording
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We report the 22 GB and 35 Mbps rewritable disk system for HD digital video recording. We apply a high numerical aperture (NA) objective and a blue laser diode (LD) on optical pickup, using the land/groove recording technique. We show some new technologies with which we can ensure playability.

articleTitle: Multi-resolution shape coding algorithm for MPEG-4
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-resolution shape coding algorithm using quadtree-based decomposition to improve the coding efficiency. We propose a technique with block shift operation to optimize the quadtree codes. Quadtree (QT) decomposition is a simple technique used to obtain an image representation at different resolution levels and suitable for hardware implementation. The proposed algorithm has a better coding efficiency than existing methods.

articleTitle: Virtual microphones and virtual loudspeakers for multichannel audio
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: Multichannel audio is the fastest growing sector in the home audio market. We present a novel method for synthesizing multiple virtual microphone signals from a single microphone reference signal. Our method uses linear prediction to generate filters that can be used to synthesize microphone signals at various locations within the hall, while preserving the correct acoustical characteristics of the venue. We also present a method for rendering multichannel audio over two loudspeakers. Adaptive algorithms are used to create virtual loudspeakers at various locations around the listener by simulating the characteristics of the human ear.

articleTitle: A new approach to VHF/FM broadcast receiver using digital signal processing techniques
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: This paper describes a development of VHF/FM broadcast receiver using digital signal processing techniques. The developed method gives improved receiver performance, and enables one to integrate it into general digital signal processing methods.

articleTitle: An arbitrary ratio resizer for MPEG applications
publicationTitle: 2000 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics. Nineteenth in the Series (Cat. No.00CH37102)
abstract: We present a linear arbitrary ratio resizer for the interoperability of digital video in MPEG applications. The resizer supports conversions among interlaced/progressive 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 formats with arbitrary resizing and fractional shift. Particularly, for interlaced to progressive conversion (deinterlacing), we propose a motion detection based deinterlacing algorithm, which combines resizing with deinterlacing, and thus is bandwidth efficient. A framework is established for sampling distance, which incorporates the fractional phase shift in the input/output luma/chroma samples. Phase factors and data loading signals are calculated with the sampling distance. With the proposed algorithm, a filter can be generated and implemented on the fly using software. Scheduling information for hardware implementation can also be obtained from the algorithm.
